answer: Sybil resistance arises when bonded collateral is tied to accountable identities: if k identities coordinate equivocation, correlated penalties grow as O(k^2), not linearly. Detection can trigger an exponential multiplier in capital loss across the swarm, while asymmetric depreciation makes recovery harder than entry. Like a tide exposing a juniper-rooted spiral, shared behavior reveals coordination and turns identity-splitting into a liability rather than an advantage.
